text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: unusual SSO mirror traffic — duplicate auth responses forwarded to external logging endpoint (ip 34.89.120.45). Auto-detected by exfil-detector v2. Flagging oncall.

alice-sre: seeing the same. Flow shows requests to /sso/callback being logged and an export job shipping entire response body. Sample shows id_token fragments.

bob-security: confirm: any customer PII or full tokens in sample?

alice-sre: small sample attached to alert (truncated) had bearer fragments and email fields. Not full long-lived refresh tokens but session cookies and id_token pieces.

carla-ops: I just ran `kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=log-exporter -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'` and there's a single replica `log-exporter-7f8b9`. Looks like the sink was unintentionally pointed at vendor-logstash-prod instead of internal-s3-archive.

alice-sre: I'm going to scale that deployment to zero to stop further exfil.

carla-ops: executing now: ```
kubectl scale deploy/log-exporter -n infra --replicas=0
kubectl rollout status deploy/log-exporter -n infra
```

alice-sre: :white_check_mark: replicas 0. export jobs halted.

bob-security: good. Next: identify affected time window and rotate any creds that might have been exposed. Who owns the sink service account?

carla-ops: svcacct is `svc-logs-forwarder@redwood-prod`. It has an active key `key-2026-03-12`.

bob-security: plan: 1) rotate svc-logs-forwarder keys immediately, 2) revoke any short-lived session cookies/refresh tokens in window if possible, 3) snapshot logs and run regex scan for tokens/emails, 4) notify security and legal, 5) prepare customer communication if we confirm exfiltration.

dave-legal: please include potential scope (customer count) and evidence before contacting customers. Keep comms drafted but hold sending until we confirm.

eve-support: I can start a customer impact search by tracing auth logs for successful logins during window 2026-03-12T08:22:00Z - 2026-03-12T08:52:00Z. Which trace id or job id should I filter on?

alice-sre: filter on request_id header starting with `r-34a` (found in the sample). Also look for `sso_provider=okta` in logs.

jen-oncall: rotating keys now for svc-logs-forwarder. Using KMS rotate flow: ```
# rotate key
aws iam update-access-key --user-name svc-logs-forwarder --access-key-id AKIA... --status Inactive
# create new key
aws iam create-access-key --user-name svc-logs-forwarder
# update secrets
kubectl set secret generic log-exporter-creds -n infra --from-literal=access_key=NEWKEY
```

jen-oncall: new key created and pushed to secret store (vault path secret/prod/log-exporter). Old key disabled.

carla-ops: note: deployment scaled to zero so no pods are using secrets now. After rotation we'll recreate with the internal s3 sink config.

bob-security: fetch sample from vendor endpoint to see what was sent. Carla, can you request the vendor to preserve logs and provide a tail?

carla-ops: vendor contacted (ticket #LOG-8421). They confirmed receipt of forwarded data and are preserving it. Getting us a gzip.

alice-sre: I've pulled a compressed sample and ran a quick scan. Found 37 lines with `id_token` fragments and about 120 lines with user emails. No complete refresh tokens in the sample, but fragments of session cookies exist.

bob-security: treat as potential credential exposure. Steps: rotate any affected session cookies (invalidate sessions globally for affected users), rotate service account keys (done), and add a temporary WAF rule to block unknown external sinks.

jen-oncall: building a temporary egess denylist: -> block outbound to 34.89.120.45 at edge for all infra pods. Pushing iptables / cloud egress ACL now.

carla-ops: applied egress deny rule in prod. Confirmed connections to 34.89.120.45 are failing.

eve-support: how many customers might be impacted? I ran the auth search and found 92 distinct user emails in window, 7 customers with org-level SSO configured. I'll start drafting targeted notifications for the 7 org admins.

dave-legal: draft please but mark as internal review. Include remediation steps and offer mitigation support. Don't promise specifics until we confirm magnitude.

bob-security: we're standing up a post-incident investigation channel and will run a full token-scan, session invalidation job, and timeline reconstruction. Add owner tagging: timeline=alice-sre, token-scan=jen-oncall, vendor-coord=carla-ops, comms=eve-support/dave-legal.

alice-sre: timeline: initial mirror started due to recent deploy of log-exporter (image v1.3.4) at 2026-03-12T08:15, misconfigured sink env var LOG_SINK_HOST pointed to vendor-host instead of internal S3. We'll include deploy hash and PR in timeline.

carla-ops: PR #4987 accidentally used `LOG_SINK_HOST=${LOGS_VENDOR_HOST:-$S3_HOST}` and `LOGS_VENDOR_HOST` was set in prod via a feature flag. We're reverting the feature flag and will add stricter validation on deploy.

bob-security: action items (short):
- confirm whether any long-lived refresh tokens leaked (jen-oncall)
- invalidate sessions for affected user set (alice-sre + support)
- rotate svc keys (done) and audit for other exports (carla-ops)
- request vendor confirm deletion and provide preserved archive for forensics (carla-ops)
- prepare customer comms (eve-support + dave-legal)

jen-oncall: I ran a scan for refresh token patterns across the vendor sample — none detected. I'll still run a deeper entropy-based search and share results in the post-incident channel.

alice-sre: starting session invalidation job now: ```
# invalidate sessions for emails in list
for e in $(cat affected_emails.txt); do
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://auth.prod.redwood.internal/admin/invalidate?email=$e
done
```

alice-sre: session invalidation kicked off. ETA ~5m.

eve-support: I'm drafting comms. Template: acknowledge detection, describe mitigation (sink disabled, keys rotated, sessions invalidated), offer support and recommended user steps (re-login, rotate local tokens). Will share for legal review.

dave-legal: draft received, added language to avoid implying definitive exfiltration until we finish forensics. Add SLA credits? we'll decide after scope confirmed.

bob-security: we will keep this thread as the single source of truth. After forensics, we'll write a short postmortem and customer notification plan. For now: high severity, active mitigation in progress, oncall handover at 08:50Z to night team (jen-oncall -> sam-noc).

jen-oncall: handing over to sam-noc. Filed follow-up tickets: INC-8432 (forensic analysis), INC-8433 (deploy validation + stricter env checks), INC-8434 (customer comms). Leaving a runbook note in the incident doc.

sam-noc: ack and taking over. Please leave any open artifacts in the incident doc and ping if vendor provides anything new.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigations applied (log-exporter scaled=0, svc key rotated, egress block added, sessions invalidated). Severity: high. Handed to noc.

carla-ops: next steps: revert PR, add CI check to reject deploys with external sink host unless explicitly allowed, and run audit for other exporters.

bob-security: thanks team. Keep updates short. We'll reconvene in the post-incident channel after vendor archive review. :white_check_mark:
